entry_points.text: Agent handling and rename hooks run in filesystem context. The agent handler exits early when unconfigured, snapshots paths, resolves hierarchy-relative paths and launches synchronously; rename rejects newlines, non-directories and cross-parent moves, with tracing on success.

Legacy filesystem behavior and boot policy define mount entry. A syscall table covers rename, options, directory creation, removal and path rendering; mount requires administrative capability; early options disable version-one support globally or by token list and control process-listing visibility.
Statistics flushing is callable from tracing contexts and ignores nonparticipating states, with base flushing via a weak hook defaulting to no operation.

exports.text: Query helpers render paths, census tasks, derive roots and resolve effective state. Path queries are thread-safe; statistics counts members by state; roots follow kernfs private links; effective lookup climbs parents in borrowed or referenced form; file handlers map to self or subsystem slots.

Helper launch allocates a descriptor from path plus argument and environment vectors, then queues work. One entry selects allocation mode; setup attaches work and hooks; execution validates path, handles detached versus waiting modes with modifiers, and releases exactly once.

Roots are initialized, published and reclaimed with identifier allocation and controller rebinding. Setup preallocates links, creates and populates kernfs roots, binds subsystems and links css sets; teardown defers freeing; rebinding validates masks then migrates controllers with updates and notifications.

Traversal, statistics and deferred work support iteration. Child walk tolerates release via serial search; rstat init prepares per-processor state; flush drains updates; base accounting aggregates times; RCU work defers freeing; pressure predicate gates optional files; v1 lookup finds groups by identifier.

hazards.text: Rebinding, enabling, publication, iteration and dying guard safety. Moves refuse non-root state unless implicit and refuse non-default to non-default moves; failures warn; partial batches unwind atomically; released cursors use serial search; killed notification precedes dying marking with parents retained.

Setup, flush and collection fail safely. Setup warns on bad inodes, lifetime errors or counts and unwinds before publication; flush may sleep and avoids non-sleepable regions; statistics rejects wrong filesystems; agent skips on empty config; pid-list queue failure is fatal.

Mount vocabulary, agent environment and lifecycle flags are fixed ABI. Flags include all, clone_children, cpuset_v2_mode, none, noprefix, xattr, favordynmods, nofavordynmods plus name and release_agent strings; agent uses HOME root and standard search path; flag families track visibility, online, dying, placement and writability.

File-name, notification and feature constants are fixed. Maximum control-file length combines type and file-type limits plus separators; minimum notification interval derives from timer frequency divided by one hundred rounded up; optional features track pressure support with a disable mask.

invariants.text: Directory publication and file presentation are deterministic. Population is idempotent and marks visible only after full success; self states gain base plus pressure entries, others gain subsystem collections; placement skips mismatched scope; prefixes and modes derive from flavor and handlers; visibility follows enablement.

Version-one mounts use a fixed flag and string vocabulary with strict consistency. Parsing falls back to source parsing then matches legacy names; agent and name forbid repeats with namespace, capability and character rules; consistency intersects masks and forbids conflicts; reconfiguration forbids flag or name changes on populated hierarchies.

Default-hierarchy control flows from propagation to enablement to migration. Effective sets inherit parent enables with threaded and implicit restrictions; subtree computation closes dependencies until stable; application creates missing states and populates directories; migration collects live sources, skips locking when empty, moves tasks and finalizes.

Statistics participation and tree shape are constrained. Only self states and flush-capable subsystems track; new roots start with inode one, self ancestor, single group and empty children; default root uses static per-processor storage; pending updates form bottom-up trees where marked nodes imply marked ancestors.

locks.text: A global group mutex serializes creation, publication, control and teardown. File updates, identifier assignment, linkage, online promotion, dying marking and teardown require ownership; path work nests css-set spin inside it; rename drops kernfs protection before acquiring it due to rank.

Identifiers and css sets use fine-grained spinning. Identifier tables use bottom-half-safe spinning with preload; removal uses a dedicated bottom-half-safe lock; css-set linkage and populated updates use interrupt-safe spinning, nested inside read-side protection.

Statistics, agent path and helper counting bound hold times. Per-subsystem interrupt-safe locks guard updates and flush construction, reacquired per processor; agent path uses a dedicated spinlock; helper count increments on entry and wakes waiters when the last exits, held across disable check and wait.

state_machines.text: Subsystem state moves from allocation through linkage and publication to teardown. After setup it joins parent lists, becomes reachable via online promotion, gains directory presence when visible, then is marked dying with directory teardown, reference killing with confirmation, and grace-deferred freeing.

Control updates use save, attempt and settle over subtrees. On failure prior control, mask and domain values are restored and propagated; a disable pass then removes states that lost membership or clears directories that became invisible, invoking reset hooks where present.

Root selection and mount acquisition validate, wait and publish. Legacy choice waits for dying subsystems with restart when references are unavailable, reuses matching roots or allocates fresh roots initially; mount checks privilege, drains offline groups, builds trees outside locks and restarts after delay when dying.

Statistics progress from lockless backlog insertion to pending-tree formation to ordered flushing. Backlog drains at collection start; bottom-up trees order roots ahead of descendants; flush walks processors under per-subsystem locks with yields between processors.

structs.text: States and groups form trees with lifecycle storage. State nodes carry identifiers, serial order, flags, references, tallies, statistics and deferred work with parent linkage; groups carry kernfs linkage, root pointers, self state, slots, masks with rollback copies, domain pointers, limits, dying counts and release work.

Statistics nodes, base counters and subsystem metadata have fixed layouts. Per-processor nodes carry sibling-child links, backlog nodes and flush pointers; base counters mirror times, runtime and notifications in current, last and subtree accumulators; metadata builds pointer, name and key tables from a repeated include.
